ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify latest 10-K/10-Q for recurring revenue percentage, customer count, trading-partner count, customer concentration, net retention, retailer mandates, module attach rates, and whether tariff/macro softness affects only discretionary modules or the core EDI subscription base.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source confirmation of current recurring revenue mix, trading-partner scale, net retention, module-level growth, and whether 2026 slowdown reflects temporary discretionary pullback or structural deceleration.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Best fit for the Serenity chokepoint lens in this chunk: a direct retail trading-partner network with recurring revenue, supplier compliance workflows, retailer-specific integrations, and operational switching costs. Demand is tied to retailer-supplier connectivity rather than discretionary consumer spending alone.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as vertical SaaS or supply-chain software rather than consumer infrastructure; market debate may overemphasize growth deceleration while underweighting embedded retailer-specific compliance and EDI workflows.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine how much revenue is tied to retail/ecommerce B2B messaging versus customs, routing, transportation management, acquisitions, and non-retail verticals.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Consumer/retail exposure is plausible but not yet quantified; need segment, vertical, and product-line evidence to confirm materiality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong adjacent consumer-infrastructure candidate because logistics data networks, carrier connectivity, customs, and trade-compliance software become more important as retail supply chains grow more complex and tariff-sensitive.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually categorized as logistics or trade-compliance software, which can cause consumer and ecommerce screens to miss its role in retail shipment, customs, and fulfillment-chain data exchange.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail/apparel share, endpoint IC volumes, reader gateway adoption, pricing, inventory correction status, patent/IP position, and dependence on large inlay/label partners.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that retail/apparel item-level tagging is a material and accelerating contributor rather than a cyclical RFID inventory recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Niche public-market pure play on RAIN RFID endpoint ICs, readers, and item-level tagging. It scores high on supplier scarcity and underfollowed discovery because retail adoption can be hidden inside a semiconductor/RFID classification.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually treated as a semiconductor or RFID technology name rather than a consumer-infrastructure beneficiary of item-level inventory accuracy, retail compliance, apparel tagging, and logistics traceability.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify FY2025 and 2026 filings for retail/wholesale revenue mix, cloud subscription growth, RPO, migration uplift, implementation backlog, and competitive displacement risk from SAP, Oracle, Blue Yonder, and private OMS/WMS vendors.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source validation of current cloud migration runway, retail/wholesale mix, RPO durability, and implementation-partner bottlenecks.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Reference leader for omnichannel order management, warehouse execution, store fulfillment, inventory availability, and cloud migration. High public-market purity and strong demand durability make it a benchmark for the whole consumer-infrastructure software layer.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Its consumer exposure is operational rather than brand-facing, and it can be classified as warehouse management or enterprise software rather than consumer infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify ARR, customer concentration, enterprise QSR wins, payments attach, hardware/service mix, acquisition integration, retention, and path to sustained free cash flow.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source verification from filings and earnings materials on ARR mix, customer wins, retention, gross margin by segment, payments attach, and acquisition integration performance.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: PAR has relatively pure exposure to restaurant operating infrastructure across POS, loyalty, ordering, back-office, and payments. The Serenity-relevant signal is that enterprise QSR and restaurant chains may treat integrated operating systems as mission-critical workflow infrastructure rather than discretionary software. It ranks above Toast because it is smaller, more vertically specific, and more likely to be overlooked due to acquisition integration and legacy-business complexity.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Smaller and more vertically specific than Toast, with a messy history and acquisition integration questions that can obscure enterprise restaurant software exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify module attach, order volume trends, enterprise customer retention, delivery marketplace dependency, ARPU, churn, and whether digital-order growth persists as dine-in normalizes.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation that order volume, module attach, retention, and ARPU are improving independently of pandemic-era delivery normalization.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Olo is a narrow public-market vehicle for enterprise restaurant digital ordering, marketplace delivery integration, payments, and guest-data workflows. The potential chokepoint is not generic restaurant demand, but the integration layer between restaurant brands, ordering channels, delivery marketplaces, and customer data systems. It has strong underfollowed-discovery value because it can be misclassified as a post-pandemic delivery-growth story rather than restaurant transaction infrastructure.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Can be dismissed as post-pandemic delivery software even though the integration layer may remain mission-critical for enterprise restaurant chains.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify latest filings for Walmart-related concentration, backlog quality, deployment timing, gross margin trajectory, working-capital needs, system acceptance risk, and whether growth extends beyond the anchor customer.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that growth can broaden beyond anchor-customer deployment cycles and that margins/backlog conversion remain durable.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Strong reference leader for retailer warehouse automation, robotic fulfillment, deployment timing, backlog conversion, and customer concentration analysis. Scores well on purity and falsifiability but lower on underfollowed discovery.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not meaningfully underfollowed in robotics discussions; included mainly as a benchmark for retailer automation bottlenecks and customer concentration risk.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify post-separation revenue mix, recurring software share, customer retention, debt maturity, hardware margin drag, self-checkout demand, and free-cash-flow conversion.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need post-separation segment disclosure proving recurring software quality, retention, leverage runway, and whether hardware/self-checkout exposure is a drag or a durable installed-base moat.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: NCR Voyix has potentially valuable embedded exposure to retail and restaurant POS, self-checkout, digital ordering, and back-office systems. It scores well on mispricing and underfollowed discovery because separation complexity, leverage, hardware legacy, and turnaround framing may obscure recurring software and embedded customer workflows. It is speculative because the same complexity that creates discovery value also creates real balance-sheet and execution risk.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Spin/separation complexity, hardware legacy, debt, and turnaround framing can obscure embedded retail/restaurant software exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify customer concentration with large retailers, category mix, private-label share gains, capacity utilization, input-cost pass-through, service levels, and margin normalization.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that private-label share gains and retailer demand are translating into sustained volume, pricing, service-level improvement, and margin recovery rather than merely cyclical food-manufacturing rebound.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: TreeHouse is a second-order consumer candidate tied to private-label food manufacturing, retailer margin strategy, and consumer trade-down. It is not a software chokepoint, but it may be a capacity and service-level bottleneck for retailers expanding private-label penetration. The thesis is testable through category volume, retailer concentration, service levels, margin normalization, and capacity utilization.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Messy food-manufacturing label and restructuring history can hide retailer private-label leverage if trade-down persists.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify order volumes, agency versus direct mix, expense flexibility, market share, commercial title exposure, regulatory risk, and rate sensitivity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current order-volume trend, margin flexibility, agency/direct economics, and evidence that market share or expense discipline can offset housing-cycle weakness.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Despite a slightly higher raw score than some higher-ranked names, Stewart is ranked fourth because its housing-cycle sensitivity is high and evidence still needs verification. It remains attractive for Serenity research because it is a smaller, cleaner title and settlement rail with potential operating leverage if housing transaction volumes normalize.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Smaller title-insurance name with cyclical housing exposure can be missed by broader consumer screens and by software-focused infrastructure screens.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail/ecommerce end-market mix, RFID growth, channel inventories, scanner/mobile-computer replacement cycle, services/software attach, and exposure to retailer capex deferrals.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current evidence that retail/RFID demand is improving enough to offset hardware-cycle and channel-inventory risks.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Important reference asset for barcode scanning, RFID, mobile computing, store operations, warehouse execution, and retail inventory accuracy. Useful for validating whether RFID and retail device replacement cycles are improving.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually treated as an industrial hardware cycle name rather than as a beneficiary of retailer inventory accuracy, RFID mandates, and omnichannel fulfillment complexity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify subscriber growth, ARPU, dealer concentration, hardware versus SaaS margin, commercial expansion, churn, and housing-turnover sensitivity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary filings and earnings-call evidence on SaaS/service revenue mix, retention, dealer concentration, ARPU trend, and how much growth is independent of new housing turnover.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Connected-property software has a clearer recurring-revenue infrastructure angle than most discretionary consumer names. The dealer network, subscriber base, monitoring workflows, and smart-home/security integrations create a plausible service rail tied to housing, property management, and home automation rather than one-time device sales.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as security hardware or smart-home exposure, while the more interesting signal is the recurring software and dealer-enabled distribution rail.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify purchase/refi mix, title order volumes, commercial exposure, title margins, regulatory risk, data/software assets, and sensitivity to mortgage rates.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level evidence separating cyclical title volume from durable data/software or settlement infrastructure economics.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Title, escrow, settlement, property data, and transaction workflow exposure maps to a regulated housing transaction rail. The business is cyclical, but the infrastructure role is hard to replicate because housing transactions require trusted data, title records, underwriting, and closing processes.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Cyclical title-insurance classification can obscure its role as regulated transaction infrastructure for home sales, refinancing, and real-estate data workflows.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify intelligent-label revenue, RFID unit growth, retail mandate exposure, apparel versus food/logistics mix, margin profile, and sensitivity to packaging inventory destocking.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need disaggregated intelligent-label and RFID economics to separate structural adoption from cyclical label-material recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Relevant to the physical data layer of consumer infrastructure: labels, RFID inlays, intelligent labels, packaging inputs, apparel tagging, food/logistics traceability, and retail compliance.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as packaging/materials rather than inventory-data infrastructure; intelligent-label exposure can be obscured by broader cyclical label-material volumes.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify revenue mix by end market, retail/logistics/food traceability exposure, recurring consumables mix, gross margins, distribution channels, and customer concentration.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that consumer traceability, retail compliance, or logistics labeling is material rather than incidental within a broader industrial identification business.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Interesting low-attention candidate one step away from the obvious theme: identification, labeling, safety, compliance, warehouse operations, food safety, and traceability workflows.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Messy industrial classification can hide exposure to consumer traceability, warehouse labeling, safety, logistics, and compliance workflows.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm whether Feedonomics revenue, retention, enterprise penetration, marketplace-channel adoption, liquidity, debt, churn, and rebranding execution are strong enough to offset broader ecommerce platform weakness.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level proof that product-feed and marketplace-integration revenue is large, retained, growing, and strategically distinct from weaker ecommerce-platform demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Commerce.com is a speculative exception because product-feed management and marketplace-channel integration can be hidden ecommerce plumbing for brands and retailers operating across Amazon, Walmart, Target+, Google, Meta, TikTok, eBay, and other channels. Its micro-cap status, rebranding, and broader ecommerce-platform weakness make it high-risk, but the Feedonomics-style integration signal is narrow enough to verify.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Below-USD-300M exception with a messy identity after BigCommerce/Commerce.com rebranding; may be screened as distressed ecommerce software rather than integration infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify location growth, net retention, GPV sensitivity to restaurant traffic, fintech margins, hardware subsidy economics, churn in SMB cohorts, and international expansion quality.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current operating metrics showing whether growth comes from durable location/module/payment expansion or from cyclical restaurant traffic and fintech monetization.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Toast remains useful as the reference leader for restaurant POS, payments, payroll, ordering, loyalty, and workflow software. Its product breadth and vertical purity make it important for benchmarking adoption, payments attach, net retention, GPV sensitivity, and SMB restaurant health. It is not the best underfollowed idea in this chunk because attention is already high and the thesis is more widely understood.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed, but useful as a reference for restaurant commerce software and SMB adoption cycles.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail-media exposure, CTV/social growth, retention, pricing, platform dependency, advertiser budget sensitivity, and competition from DoubleVerify and walled gardens.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need hard evidence of retail-media contribution, platform partner durability, net retention, pricing power, and differentiation versus DoubleVerify and in-house walled-garden measurement.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: IAS is a second-order consumer infrastructure candidate: ad verification, media quality, and measurement become more important as retail media, CTV, social, and performance advertising budgets require proof of quality and brand safety. The small-cap profile gives it strong underfollowed-discovery value.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Ad-tech classification and budget cyclicality can hide its role as trust and measurement infrastructure for consumer advertising and retail media.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Quantify Business Network revenue, growth, margins, retention, retail/consumer-goods mix, and whether this node is material enough to affect consolidated OpenText results.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Materiality is the central issue; consumer/retail business-network exposure may be too diluted to matter at the consolidated level.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potential hidden exposure to B2B integration, EDI standards, supplier digitization, and business-network workflows inside a diversified enterprise-software company.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Trading-partner network exposure is hidden inside a diversified software company whose public narrative often centers on content management, cybersecurity, IT operations, or Micro Focus integration.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify customer quality, churn, payments penetration, gross margin, sales efficiency, SMB bankruptcy exposure, product simplification, and path to durable free cash flow.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that customer quality, churn, and payments attach are improving enough to offset SMB cyclicality and competitive POS/payment pressure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lightspeed has consumer-commerce infrastructure exposure through SMB retail and restaurant POS, payments, inventory, and omnichannel tools. It is less compelling as a chokepoint than PAR or Olo because SMB POS is competitive and churn-sensitive, but its messy post-COVID narrative may create an underfollowed path if payments penetration, customer quality, and free-cash-flow durability improve.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Messy post-COVID software narrative, SMB cyclicality, and profitability concerns can hide potential value in payments attach and embedded commerce workflows.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify food/beverage exposure, private-label share, pricing versus input costs, volume elasticity, debt, customer concentration, and sustainability-driven substitution from plastic.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that consumer-packaging demand and sustainability substitution are driving durable volume and margin resilience rather than a normal cyclical packaging recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Graphic Packaging is a second-order consumer infrastructure candidate through paperboard packaging for food, beverage, household products, and foodservice. The chokepoint is weaker than restaurant software, but packaging can be operationally critical for branded and private-label shelf presence. It is worth tracking if sustainability-driven substitution from plastic, private-label growth, or foodservice packaging demand creates durable volume and pricing power.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually screened as cyclical packaging rather than as consumer-brand and private-label shelf infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify order growth, frequency, take rate, advertising revenue, grocer retention, profitability by cohort, competition from first-party retailer apps, and shopper labor costs.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that retail media and grocery technology are large enough, recurring enough, and defensible enough to offset delivery-marketplace cyclicality and competition.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: The more durable research angle is not grocery delivery alone, but grocery ecommerce, retail media, ad targeting, and grocer technology infrastructure. If advertising and enterprise/grocer tools grow faster than delivery marketplace volume, the market may be misclassifying the asset.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: May be dismissed as a pandemic delivery marketplace, while the potential hidden rail is grocery retail media and retailer technology enablement.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify current market cap, retail segment mix, scanner/mobile-computer cycle, margin recovery, debt, channel inventory, customer concentration, and competitive position versus Zebra and Honeywell.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Evidence quality is currently weak; requires primary filings to confirm current financial condition and retail exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potential obscure consumer-infrastructure candidate through barcode readers, mobile computers, sensors, machine vision, and retail/industrial automation. Non-US listing and industrial labeling may create discovery value.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Non-US listing, smaller scale, and industrial automation classification can hide retail store, logistics, scanning, and automation exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail/ecommerce revenue mix, order intake, backlog, service revenue, automation demand, capex-delay exposure, and competitive position in automated storage and retrieval systems.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current order-intake and backlog evidence, plus proof that retail/ecommerce is a material driver.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Potential niche automated storage, retrieval, and intralogistics exposure tied to warehouse density, ecommerce fulfillment, and retail distribution modernization.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Swiss-listed intralogistics supplier may be missed by US consumer, ecommerce, and robotics screens despite possible exposure to fulfillment-density needs.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify retail-media partnerships, CTV/social mix, net retention, pricing, advertiser concentration, platform API dependency, and incremental budget capture.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary evidence that retail media, CTV, and social measurement growth can sustain overall revenue despite advertiser budget cyclicality and platform dependency.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: DoubleVerify is a cleaner and more visible reference point for media verification and measurement than IAS, but its higher attention level slightly reduces discovery value. It is still worth tracking as a benchmark for whether retail media and CTV verification are durable infrastructure or cyclical ad-tech spend.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Viewed as ad-tech rather than consumer-demand infrastructure; cyclicality may overshadow durable measurement requirements.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify protective versus food packaging mix, ecommerce volumes, raw material pass-through, pricing power, debt, and margin recovery.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment-level evidence that food packaging and ecommerce damage-reduction workflows are large and resilient enough to offset cyclicality, debt, and input-cost pressure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Sealed Air has exposure to protective packaging, food packaging, ecommerce shipment protection, and damage-reduction workflows. It is operationally relevant but less pure than software names and likely more exposed to raw material, volume, and leverage cycles. It stays in the research set because food safety and ecommerce packaging can be more durable than a simple cyclical-packaging screen suggests.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often viewed as a cyclical packaging name, while food packaging and ecommerce damage-reduction workflows can be operationally critical.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify consumer packaging revenue share, pricing pass-through, resin/paper input costs, customer concentration, acquisition integration, and leverage.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer disclosure on consumer-packaging revenue share, private-label/food exposure, pricing pass-through, and whether leverage or acquisition integration weakens the setup.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Sonoco has potential consumer-staples and food-packaging exposure, but the thesis is less pure and less severe as a bottleneck than restaurant software or specialized private-label manufacturing. It remains a watchlist candidate where the key question is whether consumer-packaging resilience is being hidden by broader industrial-packaging cyclicality.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Cyclical industrial packaging label may obscure consumer-packaging resilience and private-label shelf exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify residential marketplace investment drag, Apartments.com growth, commercial data retention, sales efficiency, and competitive spend versus Zillow/Realtor.com.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current segment-level data on residential marketplace spend, Apartments.com growth, commercial data retention, and whether residential investment is creating or destroying incremental returns.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: CoStar is useful as a reference leader for real-estate data, rental marketplaces, and housing discovery rails, but it ranks lower because the chunk is explicitly seeking underfollowed Serenity candidates. Its role is more benchmark than alpha-discovery candidate.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included to benchmark housing-data rails, marketplace economics, residential investment drag, and competitive spend versus smaller vertical or transaction-infrastructure names.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify organic growth, churn, home-services mix, payments attach, debt, acquisition integration, customer acquisition cost, and exposure to home improvement cyclicality.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that home-services software is material, organic growth is healthy, churn is controlled, payments attach is improving, and leverage does not dominate the equity story.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: EverCommerce has a plausible hidden housing-services rail through contractor, home-services, payments, and SMB workflow software, but the roll-up structure, mixed verticals, debt, and organic-growth uncertainty keep it below cleaner infrastructure candidates.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Roll-up structure, mixed verticals, SMB exposure, and lower liquidity can hide home-services software rails.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify solvency, insurance claims exposure, segment profitability, customer acquisition economics, data advantage, debt, dilution risk, and whether home-services demand is durable.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need immediate verification of balance-sheet runway, insurance loss exposure, segment profitability, cash burn, dilution risk, and whether any data advantage is economically real.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Porch is included only as a speculative exception because it sits near moving, home-services, home-insurance, and home-data workflows. Potential upside to the hidden rail is high, but solvency, insurance claims, dilution, governance, and segment profitability risks dominate the research setup.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Micro-cap/speculative exception with governance, insurance, and balance-sheet complexity; included only because it sits near under-mapped home-services and home-data workflows.

summary: Split Layer 3 ranking merged from candidate chunks.
